briefs.synergy_brouwer_2019:
Topic: Psychological Predictors of MDD Relapse
Objective: Identify prospective longitudinal studies that test whether baseline psychological factors (cognitive, personality, behavioral, or interpersonal) predict the future recurrence or relapse of Major Depressive Disorder (MDD) in individuals who are currently in remission or recovered. The review seeks to validate specific theoretical models of vulnerability by examining if these factors precede a new depressive episode confirmed by clinical assessment.
Problem being solved: Determine if the study measures a psychological predictor at baseline in a remitted MDD population and tracks them forward in time to observe a subsequent episode of MDD, excluding studies focused on treatment efficacy, symptom severity changes without diagnostic recurrence, or non-MDD populations.
Must-include terms: major depressive disorder, recurrence, relapse, prospective, longitudinal, predictor, remission, recovered, follow-up, vulnerability, risk factor, survival analysis, hazard ratio, time-to-event, incident episode
Nice-to-have terms: cognitive reactivity, dysfunctional attitudes, rumination, neuroticism, personality traits, extreme response style, mindfulness-based cognitive therapy, continuation therapy, residual symptoms, life events, attachment style, metacognitive awareness
Exclusion terms: bipolar disorder, psychosis, schizophrenia, ultra-high risk, substance use, cannabis, alcohol, smoking cessation, pathological gambling, migraine, chronic pain, spinal cord stimulation, cancer, infertility, postpartum depression only, cross-sectional, prevalence, symptom severity only, treatment efficacy trial, randomized controlled trial of intervention, neuroimaging, biomarker, cortisol, gene expression, transcriptomics, inflammation, animal model, review, meta-analysis, protocol, case report, psychoanalytic case study, normal adolescents, general population without MDD history
Industry: Clinical Psychology and Psychiatry
Application: Prediction of Major Depressive Disorder Recurrence
Technology focus: cognitive theories of depression, personality-based vulnerability models, behavioral activation theories, interpersonal stress models, diathesis-stress frameworks, metacognitive models, prospective cohort designs, survival analysis methods
briefs.synergy_leenaars_2020:
Topic: Methotrexate RA Trial Design Comparison
Objective: Identify primary efficacy studies (randomized controlled trials or controlled animal experiments) evaluating methotrexate as an intervention for rheumatoid arthritis. The review compares experimental design features (e.g., randomization, blinding, sample size, sex distribution) between preclinical animal models and human clinical trials.
Problem being solved: Determine if the paper reports original empirical data on the efficacy of methotrexate in treating rheumatoid arthritis (or a validated RA animal model), explicitly excluding reviews, mechanistic-only studies without efficacy endpoints, safety/toxicity-focused papers, and studies on non-RA conditions.
Must-include terms: methotrexate, rheumatoid arthritis, MTX, collagen-induced arthritis, adjuvant-induced arthritis, CIA, AIA, randomized, placebo-controlled, efficacy, disease activity, joint swelling, synovitis
Nice-to-have terms: double-blind, clinical trial, animal model, SCID mice, humanized mice, DAS28, ACR criteria, Sharp score, erosion, remission
Exclusion terms: review, meta-analysis, systematic review, cost-effectiveness, pharmacokinetics, toxicity, safety, adverse events, psoriatic arthritis, juvenile arthritis, inflammatory bowel disease, cancer, in vitro, mechanism only, perioperative, lung function
Industry: Biomedical Research
Application: Translational research comparing preclinical and clinical trial designs in rheumatology
Technology focus: Randomized Controlled Trials, Animal Models of Arthritis, Experimental Design Methodology, Efficacy Endpoints, Translational Gap Analysis
briefs.synergy_moran_2021:
Topic: Nutritional Condition and Animal Risk-Taking
Objective: To identify experimental studies where an animal's nutritional or energetic state was actively manipulated (e.g., via diet restriction, supplementation, or fasting) and the subsequent effect on risk-taking behavior (e.g., boldness, exploration, predation avoidance) was measured. The review specifically targets tests of the asset protection principle or state-dependent safety hypothesis in non-human animals.
Problem being solved: Determine if the study experimentally alters the nutritional condition of non-human animals and measures a resulting change in risk-related behavior, excluding observational correlations, human clinical trials, livestock management reports, and studies focusing solely on food safety or medical pathology.
Must-include terms: diet manipulation, food restriction, fasting, nutritional state, energetic condition, body condition, risk-taking, boldness, predation risk, exploration behavior, foraging under risk, state-dependent, asset protection, experimental diet, hunger level
Nice-to-have terms: starvation, supplementation, caloric restriction, novelty test, open field test, predator odor, trade-off, survival probability, phenotypic plasticity, behavioral syndrome, invasive species, wildlife
Exclusion terms: human, patient, clinical trial, obesity treatment, anorexia nervosa, bariatric surgery, livestock production, agricultural yield, food safety, consumer behavior, organic food, dietary survey, epidemiology, case report, review article
Industry: Ecology and Behavioral Biology
Application: Experimental analysis of how nutritional status drives risk assessment and decision-making in animals
Technology focus: dietary manipulation experiments, behavioral assays, predation risk modeling, state-dependent life history theory, meta-analysis of behavioral traits
briefs.synergy_muthu_2021:
Topic: Fragility Index of Spine Surgery RCTs
Objective: Identify randomized controlled trials (RCTs) in spine surgery that report statistically significant dichotomous outcomes suitable for Fragility Index calculation. The review assesses the robustness of these findings by determining how many event status changes would alter statistical significance.
Problem being solved: Screen for primary prospective RCTs involving surgical interventions on the human spine with binary outcome data; exclude observational studies, non-surgical management trials, animal/cadaver studies, and papers lacking reported significant dichotomous results.

Exclusion terms: observational, cohort study, case series, meta-analysis, systematic review, animal, cadaver, specimen, rat, pig, canine, non-surgical, conservative treatment, physical therapy, injection, epidural, nerve block, pharmacological, medication, orthosis, brace, education, exercise program, pediatric, neonate, infant, oncology, tumor, osteosarcoma, trauma, fracture, infection, scoliosis correction, deformity, protocol only, study design, methodology paper, cost-effectiveness, quality of life only, continuous outcome, VAS score, ODI score, NDI score, pain score, subgroup analysis, post-hoc, secondary analysis, letter, editorial, commentary
Industry: Clinical Research / Orthopedic & Neurological Surgery

briefs.synergy_nelson_2002:
Topic: Postmenopausal HRT Primary Prevention and Symptom Management
Objective: To identify randomized controlled trials and prospective cohort studies evaluating the effects of systemic or local estrogen/progestin therapy in postmenopausal women. The review focuses on primary prevention of chronic diseases (cardiovascular, bone, cancer) and the management of menopausal symptoms (vasomotor, urogenital). Studies must compare hormone therapy against placebo or no treatment to isolate the effect of hormones.
Problem being solved: Determine if the study evaluates estrogen or progestin therapy for prevention or symptom relief in postmenopausal women, excluding studies focused on non-hormonal alternatives, secondary prevention in diseased populations, or mechanistic pilots without clinical outcomes.

Nice-to-have terms: bone mineral density, fracture, hot flushes, vasomotor symptoms, cardiovascular disease, breast cancer, quality of life, transdermal, conjugated equine estrogens, primary prevention, intact uterus, hysterectomized
Exclusion terms: premenopausal, perimenopausal only, contraception, oral contraceptive, fertility, ovarian function, androgen, testosterone, tamoxifen, raloxifene, SERM, aromatase inhibitor, anastrozole, letrozole, bisphosphonate, alendronate, soy, phytoestrogen, isoflavone, dementia treatment, Alzheimer's treatment, secondary prevention, established coronary disease, mechanistic, pilot study, review, meta-analysis, guideline, case report
Industry: Clinical Medicine
Application: Menopause management and chronic disease prevention
Technology focus: systemic hormone replacement therapy, local vaginal estrogen therapy, combined estrogen-progestin regimens, unopposed estrogen therapy, transdermal hormone delivery, oral hormone delivery
briefs.synergy_sep_2021:
Topic: Rodent Object-in-Context Task Methodology Review
Objective: To identify primary research studies in rodents that explicitly utilize the Object-in-Context (OIC) task, also known as the object-context mismatch or discrimination task, to assess context-dependent recognition memory. The review aims to analyze methodological variables (e.g., apparatus, timing, stimuli) and outcomes specifically derived from this distinct behavioral paradigm where an object's familiarity is judged relative to its background context.
Problem being solved: Determine if the study reports empirical data using the specific rodent Object-in-Context (OIC) behavioral paradigm, distinguishing it from general object recognition, spatial location tasks, or contextual fear conditioning.
Must-include terms: object-in-context, object context, context-object, object/context, mismatch, discrimination, recognition, rodent, rat, mouse, mice, hippocampus, memory, exploration, familiar
Nice-to-have terms: episodic-like, what-where-when, novel object, spontaneous preference, retrosplenial, perirhinal, entorhinal, dentate gyrus, reconsolidation, interference, delay interval, sample phase
Exclusion terms: human, clinical, patient, fMRI, virtual reality, fear conditioning, freezing, shock, aversive, spatial navigation, water maze, radial arm, T-maze, Morris, review, meta-analysis
Industry: Neuroscience / Preclinical Research
Application: Behavioral assessment of context-dependent episodic-like memory in rodents
Technology focus: Object-in-Context (OIC) task, Object-Context Mismatch task, Spontaneous object recognition variants, Hippocampal-dependent memory paradigms
briefs.synergy_van_der_valk_2021:
Topic: Hair Glucocorticoids and Anthropometry
Objective: To identify observational studies measuring endogenous long-term glucocorticoids (cortisol/cortisone) in human scalp hair and reporting their statistical association with anthropometric measures of adiposity (BMI, waist circumference, waist-hip ratio). The review focuses on cross-sectional or longitudinal correlations in general, clinical, or at-risk populations to quantify the link between chronic stress exposure and body fat distribution.
Problem being solved: Screeners must distinguish between studies that measure hair cortisol as a biomarker for obesity-related outcomes versus studies that use hair cortisol for psychiatric validation, method development, animal research, or populations where hair sampling is invalid (e.g., alopecia) or confounded by exogenous steroid therapy.
Must-include terms: hair cortisol, hair cortisone, scalp hair, body mass index, BMI, waist circumference, adiposity, obesity, anthropometric, waist-hip ratio, WHR, glucocorticoid, long-term cortisol, chronic stress, body fat
Nice-to-have terms: LC-MS, mass spectrometry, ELISA, HPA axis, DHEA, dehydroepiandrosterone, cross-sectional, cohort, metabolic syndrome, visceral fat, reference range, biomarker
Exclusion terms: alopecia, hair loss, nail cortisol, fingernail, wool cortisol, sheep, cattle, primate, monkey, marmoset, exogenous glucocorticoid, hydrocortisone replacement, Cushing's disease treatment, saliva cortisol, serum cortisol, study protocol, randomized controlled trial, intervention, supplement, case report
Industry: Clinical Endocrinology and Epidemiology
Application: Chronic Stress Biomarkers and Adiposity Assessment
Technology focus: Scalp Hair Steroid Analysis, Liquid Chromatography-Tandem Mass Spectrometry (LC-MS/MS), Enzyme-Linked Immunosorbent Assay (ELISA) for Hair, Observational Association Studies, Anthropometric Measurement
briefs.synergy_van_dis_2020:
Topic: Long-term CBT outcomes for anxiety disorders
Objective: To identify randomized controlled trials evaluating the durability of cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) and related exposure-based or cognitive interventions for anxiety disorders, PTSD, and OCD. The review specifically targets studies reporting follow-up data collected at least one month after the conclusion of active treatment to distinguish sustained effects from immediate post-treatment gains.
Problem being solved: Screeners must distinguish between trials that include a distinct post-treatment follow-up assessment period and those that only measure outcomes immediately after therapy ends or during treatment. Additionally, screeners must exclude studies focusing on non-anxiety primary diagnoses (e.g., depression, pain, insomnia), pediatric populations, or mechanistic laboratory experiments without clinical follow-up.
Must-include terms: randomized controlled trial, cognitive behavioral therapy, CBT, anxiety disorder, posttraumatic stress disorder, PTSD, obsessive-compulsive disorder, OCD, panic disorder, generalized anxiety disorder, social anxiety disorder, specific phobia, follow-up, exposure therapy, long-term
Nice-to-have terms: agoraphobia, prolonged exposure, cognitive processing therapy, acceptance and commitment therapy, metacognitive therapy, internet-based, guided self-help, relapse prevention, durability, maintenance, treatment as usual, wait-list control
Exclusion terms: children, adolescents, pediatric, depression only, major depressive disorder, insomnia, sleep, chronic pain, fibromyalgia, migraine, low back pain, cataract, intraocular lens, radiation therapy, psychosurgery, animal model, healthy volunteers, students, non-clinical, mechanism, biomarker, neuroimaging, skin conductance, CO2 challenge, protocol, study design, rationale, bereavement, grief, alcohol, substance use only, dialysis, advance care planning, yoga, melatonin, temazepam, zolpidem, Kinesio taping, magnetic field therapy, Ashwagandha
Industry: Mental Health and Psychiatry
Application: Psychotherapy efficacy and durability for anxiety-spectrum disorders
Technology focus: Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT), Exposure Therapy, Randomized Controlled Trials (RCTs), Longitudinal Follow-up Assessment, Anxiety Disorder Treatment Outcomes
